notes: The right to repair is a movement that advocates for consumers' rights to repair their own products, including access to repair manuals, tools, and parts.
This topic involves understanding legal and technological aspects, as well as practical applications and future implications.

questions.question: What is right to repair?
questions.right_answer: The right to repair means consumers have the ability to repair their own products, including access to repair manuals, tools, and parts.
wrong_answers: The right to repair means consumers can return products for free.
The right to repair means consumers can sell their old products.
The right to repair means consumers can get discounts on new products.
questions.why: Right to repair is about the ability to repair, not return or sell products.

questions.question: Why is right to repair important?
questions.right_answer: Right to repair is important because it can reduce waste, save money, and give consumers control over their products.
wrong_answers: Right to repair is important because it can increase the cost of products.
Right to repair is important because it can make products less reliable.
Right to repair is important because it can limit the use of products.
questions.why: Right to repair promotes sustainability and consumer choice.

questions.question: What are some legal challenges in right to repair?
questions.right_answer: Some legal challenges in right to repair include patent law, trade secrets, and anti-tampering laws.
wrong_answers: Some legal challenges in right to repair include tax laws and consumer protection laws.
Some legal challenges in right to repair include environmental laws and labor laws.
Some legal challenges in right to repair include data privacy laws and intellectual property laws.
questions.why: These are not specific to right to repair and do not address the technical and legal barriers.
